citations.assertion: Named Alexander of Old Court; existing family account. Burke’s Visitation, vol.2, printed armorial section p.67 (PDF 341), has now been read in the scan. It explicitly describes Alexander of Old Court, formerly Auchinraith, as eldest son of the late John Glasgow and Helen, daughter of James Smith, and grandson of Alexander Glasgow, merchant, and Agnes Monro of Edinburgh. The family passage was already quoted in the held biography; inspecting it is not discovery of a previously unknown grandfather name. The underlying Lyon matriculation remains unread. The independently identified John–Helen Smith merchant household now has inspected burgess evidence, and Burke explicitly gives its Alexander grandfather with a Monro wife associated with Edinburgh. That rare paired family description is more specific than the earlier chronological comparison with Alexander-1309’s Alexander/Mary Munro household, whose 1757 marriage was recorded in Edinburgh and Barony. The corrected 1771 Barony child fits the merchant’s possible generation. This modestly strengthens the whole existing father-profile hypothesis from 38% to 45% Possible; it does not make it Probable. Burke names Agnes Monro, not the documented Mary Munro of Alexander-1309’s couple. Their identity cannot be assumed, and the 1771 child has no inspected occupation, wife or estate bridge identifying him as the merchant rather than the Colinton account John-1304. The merchant’s circa 1770 birth is an inherited estimate, not independent corroboration. Retain both modern Johns and the current father selection, all mothers, vital fields and upstream grades. No new father attachment or merge follows. The 1741 childhood identification of Alexander-1309 is not certified by this review. Exact percentages are subjective judgements, not measured probabilities.
